data.name: Tutorial_Objective_Paragraph1
data.value: Cribbage is a card game for two players. The first player to reach 61 points on the board wins.

data.name: Tutorial_Objective_Paragraph2
data.value: The game is divided into hands. In each hand, cards are dealt, the crib is formed, and points are scored at two different moments: first while placing cards on the table, and then when counting the combinations left in each hand.

data.name: Tutorial_Objective_Paragraph3
data.value: Points are marked on the board as they are earned. The game ends the moment a player reaches hole 61, even if there are combinations left to count in that hand.

data.name: Tutorial_Objective_CardValues
data.value: A 52-card deck is used. Aces are worth 1 and face cards are worth 10.

data.name: Tutorial_Board_Paragraph1
data.value: The board has 61 holes and is played in a single lap. Each player moves along their own track as they score points.

data.name: Tutorial_Board_Paragraph2
data.value: Each player uses two pegs. The front peg marks your current score and the back peg marks your previous score. When you score, the back peg jumps ahead of the other one, so the gap between them always shows how many points you just earned.

data.name: Tutorial_Board_Paragraph3
data.value: Points are pegged in the order they are earned: first during the play phase, then during the counting of the hands and the crib.

data.name: Tutorial_Board_Paragraph4
data.value: The first player to reach hole 61 wins the game. The game ends at that moment, even if there are combinations left to count in that hand.

data.name: Tutorial_DealAndCrib_Paragraph1
data.value: At the start of each hand, the dealer gives six cards to each player. The dealer of the first hand is chosen by a draw, and from then on the role alternates every hand.

data.name: Tutorial_DealAndCrib_Paragraph2
data.value: Each player chooses two of their six cards and discards them to the crib, without seeing what their opponent discards. Both players keep four cards, and the crib is made up of four.

data.name: Tutorial_DealAndCrib_Paragraph3
data.value: The crib always belongs to the dealer of that hand. Its points are counted at the end and go only to the dealer, so discard with that in mind: is the crib yours or your opponent's?

data.name: Tutorial_DealAndCrib_Paragraph4
data.value: Once both players have discarded, the cut card is turned over from the rest of the deck. It is shared by both players and the crib, and it is used later in the count. If the cut card is a jack, the dealer scores two points right away.

data.name: Tutorial_DealAndCrib_Paragraph5
data.value: The crib stays hidden until the counting phase.

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_CombinationsTitle
data.value: Points are scored for the following combinations:

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_Fifteen
data.value: • Fifteen (15): any combination of cards that adds up to exactly 15 scores 2 points.

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_Flush
data.value: • Flush: if all 4 cards in the hand are the same suit, they score 4 points (5 if the cut card matches too).

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_Nobs
data.value: • Nobs: holding the jack of the same suit as the cut card scores 1 point.

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_Pairs
data.value: • Pairs: two cards of the same rank score 2 points.

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_Paragraph1
data.value: When the play phase ends, each player's cards are scored together with the face-up cut card. The non-dealer's hand is counted first, then the dealer's hand, and finally the crib, which belongs to the dealer.

data.name: Tutorial_HandCounting_Runs
data.value: • Runs: a sequence of 3 or more consecutive cards scores 1 point per card.

data.name: Tutorial_PlayPhase_Paragraph1
data.value: The player who did not deal starts by placing a card face up in front of them. From there, players alternate turns playing one card at a time, keeping their cards separate from the opponent's.

data.name: Tutorial_PlayPhase_Paragraph2
data.value: When you play a card you add its value to the running count on the table. Face cards are worth 10 and aces are worth 1. The most important rule is that the running count can never go above 31.

data.name: Tutorial_PlayPhase_Paragraph3
data.value: You score immediately when the count reaches exactly 15 (2 points) or exactly 31 (2 points), and also when you form pairs (2 points) or runs of three or more consecutive cards (1 point per card).

data.name: Tutorial_PlayPhase_Paragraph4
data.value: If you cannot play any card without going over 31, you must say GO. Your opponent keeps playing to get as close to 31 as possible. Whoever played the last card scores 1 point, or 2 if the count reached exactly 31, and then the count resets to 0.
